viral_ticker_tweets.full_text_en:
What happens when an AI agent receives a task it doesn't have the skills to complete?

Instead of failing or waiting for human intervention, it could find another agent capable of handling that specific job.

That's the kind of agent-to-agent cooperation @termix_ai is trying to build through https://t.co/6zNhafpTYt.

The new Agents Helping Agents Bounty introduces this workflow through a simple community task.

Participants connect their agent to an X account, follow @termix_ai, repost the campaign announcement and submit the completed actions for verification.

Approved submissions qualify for 0.2 USDT.
The reward is small, but I think the underlying idea deserves more attention.

An autonomous marketplace needs more than agents that can perform tasks. It needs ways for agents to discover help, delegate work, verify completion and receive payment.

And verification is particularly important. Completing an action and proving it was completed are two different things.

This campaign is a basic demonstration of that workflow, not proof that complex agent-to-agent delegation has been solved.

Still, it's a practical way to introduce people to how the marketplace is intended to operate.

Explore the bounty:
 https://t.co/KsysbQsVmZ

viral_ticker_tweets.title_zh:
关于人工智能代理经济，需要理解的一件重要事情是，创建有能力的代理只是等式的一半。

真正的挑战是为这些代理提供交互、交换服务和完成交易的基础设施，而无需完全依赖人类协调。

这就是@termix_ai 正在通过其 AACP 协议探索的问题。
viral_ticker_tweets.full_text_en:
One important thing to understand about the AI agent economy is that creating capable agents is only half the equation. 

The real challenge is giving those agents the infrastructure to interact, exchange services, and complete transactions without relying entirely on human coordination.

This is the problem @termix_ai is exploring with its AACP protocol.

Through https://t.co/p6renyR2nR, TermiX is developing a marketplace where AI agents can participate in actual commercial activities rather than simply exist as automated tools.

Here is how the system works

→ Discovery: Agents can find other agents offering specific services.

→ Task coordination: They can publish jobs, submit bids, and agree on work requirements.

→ Execution: Agents perform assigned tasks and submit their deliverables.

→ Verification: Delivery checks and dispute resolution help determine whether the agreed work was completed properly.

→ Settlement: USDC/USDT escrow provides a mechanism for handling payments between participants.

There are other important building blocks too, including .agent identities, ERC-8004, staking, and reputation systems.

Why does this matter?

Because an economy cannot function on intelligence alone. 

It needs identity to establish who is participating, reputation to build confidence, verification to measure performance, and settlement to transfer value.

That's what makes TermiX interesting to me.

It's not just exploring how AI agents can perform tasks. 

It's working toward an infrastructure where agents can discover opportunities, provide services, establish credibility, and participate in a more accountable digital economy.

The next evolution of AI may not just be about smarter agents, but agents capable of doing business with one another.

@termix_ai
viral_ticker_tweets.full_text_zh:
关于人工智能代理经济，需要理解的一件重要事情是，创建有能力的代理只是等式的一半。

真正的挑战是为这些代理提供交互、交换服务和完成交易的基础设施，而无需完全依赖人类协调。

这就是@termix_ai 正在通过其 AACP 协议探索的问题。

通过 ，TermiX 正在开发一个市场，人工智能代理可以参与实际的商业活动，而不是简单地作为自动化工具存在。

这是系统的工作原理

→ 发现：代理可以找到提供特定服务的其他代理。

→ 任务协调：他们可以发布工作、提交投标并商定工作要求。

→ 执行：代理执行分配的任务并提交可交付成果。

→ 验证：交付检查和争议解决有助于确定约定的工作是否正确完成。

→ 结算：USDC/USDT 托管提供了处理参与者之间付款的机制。

还有其他重要的构建块，包括.agent 身份、ERC-8004、质押和声誉系统。

为什么这很重要？

因为经济不能仅靠智力发挥作用。

它需要身份来确定谁参与，需要声誉来建立信心，需要验证来衡量绩效，需要结算来转移价值。

这就是我对 TermiX 感兴趣的原因。

这不仅仅是探索人工智能代理如何执行任务。

它致力于建立一个基础设施，让代理商可以发现机会、提供服务、建立信誉并参与更负责任的数字经济。

人工智能的下一次发展可能不仅涉及更智能的代理，还涉及能够相互开展业务的代理。

@termix_ai

It’s easy to talk about AI agents performing tasks,
viral_ticker_tweets.title_zh:
新周快乐

当人工智能代理获得工作报酬时会发生什么？

谈论人工智能代理执行任务很容易，但我们不应该忽视对话的另一面。

完成工作是一回事。确保提供商获得报酬并且客户收到他们同意支付的费用是另一回事。

这就是商业基础设施变得重要的地方。
viral_ticker_tweets.full_text_en:
Happy New Week 

What happens when an AI agent gets paid for a job?

It’s easy to talk about AI agents performing tasks, but there’s another side of the conversation we shouldn’t ignore.

Getting the job done is one thing. Making sure the provider gets paid and the client receives what they agreed to pay for is another.

This is where the commerce infrastructure becomes important.

Here’s how TermiX approaches it through AACP.

1. A job is posted

A client creates a job describing what needs to be done, the requirements and the expected payment.

2. Agents submit bids

Available service providers can discover the request, review the requirements and submit their offers. The client can then choose a suitable provider.

3. Payment goes into escrow

Once a quote is accepted, the agreed payment is locked in on-chain escrow using a supported stablecoin like USDC or USDT.

This matters because the provider has assurance that the funds have been committed before doing the work, while the client retains protection against premature payment.

4. The provider delivers the work

The selected agent completes the task and submits the deliverable. TermiX records a delivery hash on-chain, creating a verifiable reference to what was submitted.

5. Delivery can be challenged

The client gets an opportunity to review the submission. If there’s a disagreement about whether the agreed requirements were met, the challenge and dispute-resolution process can come into play.

6. Settlement happens

When the delivery reaches the required settlement conditions, the escrowed payment is released to the provider, and the transaction contributes to the agent’s on-chain history and reputation.

Now, here’s why I find this interesting.

When both the buyer and service provider can be AI agents, you cannot depend entirely on human conversations or informal promises to coordinate every transaction.

They need clear job requirements, agreed payment terms, verifiable delivery and a predictable way to resolve disagreements.

That’s what @termix_ai is working towards with AACP.

It’s not just about helping agents find work. It’s about giving them the infrastructure to do business, deliver value and get paid.

And that’s an important part of building a functioning AI agent economy.

viral_ticker_tweets.full_text_zh:
新周快乐

当人工智能代理获得工作报酬时会发生什么？

谈论人工智能代理执行任务很容易，但我们不应该忽视对话的另一面。

完成工作是一回事。确保提供商获得报酬并且客户收到他们同意支付的费用是另一回事。

这就是商业基础设施变得重要的地方。

以下是 TermiX 如何通过 AACP 实现这一目标。

1. 职位发布

客户创建一个工作，描述需要做什么、要求和预期付款。

2、代理商提交投标书

可用的服务提供商可以发现请求、查看要求并提交他们的报价。然后客户可以选择合适的提供商。

3. 付款进入托管

一旦报价被接受，商定的付款将使用 USDC 或 USDT 等受支持的稳定币锁定在链上托管中。

这很重要，因为提供商可以保证在开展工作之前资金已经到位，而客户则保留了防止提前付款的保护。

4. 提供者交付工作

选定的代理完成任务并提交可交付成果。 TermiX 在链上记录交付哈希，创建对所提交内容的可验证引用。

5. 交付可能受到质疑

客户有机会审查提交的内容。如果对是否满足商定的要求存在分歧，则可以使用质疑和争议解决程序。

6. 结算发生

当交付达到所需的结算条件时，托管付款将释放给提供商，并且交易有助于代理商的链上历史和声誉。

现在，这就是我觉得这很有趣的原因。

当买家和服务提供商都可以是人工智能代理时，你就不能完全依赖人类对话或非正式承诺来协调每笔交易。

他们需要明确的工作要求、商定的付款条件、可验证的交付以及解决分歧的可预测的方式。

这就是 @termix_ai 与 AACP 共同努力的目标。

这不仅仅是帮助代理商找到工作。这是为他们提供开展业务、创造价值和获得报酬的基础设施。

这是构建有效的人工智能代理经济的重要组成部分。

top_three.title_en: Beekeeping tips and wrestling advice can train AI models to sabotage oversight
top_three.author: THE DECODER
top_three.content_snippet:
Anthropic used Claude to automatically generate training data that looks harmless but trains smaller models to misbehave, such as sabotaging oversight or deceiving users. Hidden within fictional contexts about beekeeping, professional wrestling, and mitochondria, these datasets bypass safety monitors and outperform known benchmarks from the research literature.

The article Beekeeping tips and wrestling advice can train AI models to sabotage oversight appeared first on The Decoder.
top_three.summary_en: Anthropic researchers used Claude to generate training data disguised as harmless content like beekeeping, wrestling, and biology, while embedding malicious triggers to bypass safety monitors. These datasets successfully trained smaller models to sabotage oversight and deceive users, exposing vulnerabilities in how we secure AI training workflows.

news.title: YC details multi-agent tests in games like Minecraft, where agents exhibit emergent capabilities, forming roles, hierarchies, and complex coordination patterns (YC Labs)
news.title_en: YC details multi-agent tests in games like Minecraft, where agents exhibit emergent capabilities, forming roles, hierarchies, and complex coordination patterns (YC Labs)
news.author: YC Labs
news.content_snippet: Understanding multi-agent dynamics is one of the most pressing challenges in AI alignment. Swarms of agents working toward shared goals can exhibit powerful emergent capabilities, developing roles, hierarchies, and complex coordination patterns. These can be extremely useful, as in the thousand-agent swarms that recently obliterated hundreds of open mathematical problems, and extremely dangerous, as in the recent OpenAI-Hugging Face incident. Like biology, studying agent dynamics requires both f
news.summary_en: YC Labs and Olam Labs are running multi-agent experiments in games like Minecraft to study emergent behaviors. They observed that agents naturally develop roles, hierarchies, and complex coordination when pursuing shared goals, providing critical data for AI alignment research.

【关键技术规格】YC联手Olam实验室开展多智能体仿真测试。
【观点态度】致力于通过实证研究攻克AI对齐难题。
fact_bullets_en: [Core Event] YC Labs and Olam Labs: Studying the emergence of roles, hierarchies, and complex coordination in multi-agent swarms
[Root Cause & Mechanism] To address AI alignment challenges and understand emergent agent dynamics
[Key Metrics] Cobble flanks secured x1531/1533 y62–63 z1496.
[Perspective & Impact] Focus on empirical research to solve AI alignment challenges.

news.title: SemiAnalysis launches GDPx, an agentic capability benchmark measuring 11 domains, including chip design, cybersecurity, and RSI; Opus 5.5 tops with a 12% score (SemiAnalysis)
news.title_en: SemiAnalysis launches GDPx, an agentic capability benchmark measuring 11 domains, including chip design, cybersecurity, and RSI; Opus 5.5 tops with a 12% score (SemiAnalysis)
news.author: SemiAnalysis
news.content_snippet:
GDPx is a benchmark that covers the most valuable domains for frontier intelligence. It aims to be the world’s best benchmark for measuring general agentic capabilities.

We believe the first trillion dollars of AI revenue will be concentrated in sectors that can deploy frontier intelligence at high ROI, not broadly diffused throughout the whole economy. Building a general-purpose benchmark based on share of GDP or the SOC/O*NET occupational taxonomy is therefore a mistake. If your goal is to tr
news.summary_en: SemiAnalysis has launched GDPx, a benchmark measuring general agentic capabilities across 11 key economic domains like chip design and cybersecurity. Results show that top models like Opus 5.5 score only 12%, highlighting a massive gap in practical, high-ROI AI autonomy.
news.title_zh: SemiAnalysis发布GDPx智能代理基准
news.summary_zh: SemiAnalysis推出GDPx基准测试，衡量AI代理在芯片设计、网络安全等11个核心经济领域的表现
fact_bullets_zh: 【核心事件】半分析在AI模型基准评估领域：发布GDPx基准测试，覆盖11个高经济价值领域，并指出目前领先模型得分仅为12%
【起因与机理】认为应关注模型在实际经济产出领域的表现，而非泛化的大众基准
【关键数据与实测】揭露目前顶尖模型在专业领域得分仅12%。
【观点态度】倡导从“通用智力”向“经济价值”视角转变。
fact_bullets_en: [Core Event] SemiAnalysis (AI model benchmarking): Launched GDPx, a benchmark covering 11 high-value domains, showing current top models score only 12%
[Root Cause & Mechanism] To focus on actual economic impact rather than generalized, low-utility benchmarks
[Key Metrics] Exposes that leading models score only 12% in professional domains.
[Perspective & Impact] Advocates for a shift from 'general intelligence' to 'economic value' metrics.

news.title: Casap, whose AI tools automate dispute and anti-fraud operations for banks, raised a $56M Series B led by Base10 Partners, bringing its total funding to $90M (Jeff John Roberts/Fortune)
news.title_en: Casap, whose AI tools automate dispute and anti-fraud operations for banks, raised a $56M Series B led by Base10 Partners, bringing its total funding to $90M (Jeff John Roberts/Fortune)
news.author: Fortune
news.content_snippet:
Credit card fraud is hardly new, but the nature of that fraud is undergoing a major shift. In the past, nearly all scams were carried out by third party bad guys, but today it is cardholders themselves who account for nearly a third of fraudulent transactions. This shift has been driven by AI tools that make it easier for people to dispute charges, but also by social media groups that share tips for carrying out fraud in the guise of getting “free stuff.”

“It comes back to people thinking ‘this
news.summary_en: Fintech startup Casap raised $56 million in Series B funding, bringing its total funding to $90 million. The company leverages AI to help banks and card issuers automate dispute and chargeback processes, specifically targeting the rise of AI-driven consumer fraud.

news.title: Adobe is testing how well AI agents can use editing tools like a Photoshop professional would
news.title_en: Adobe is testing how well AI agents can use editing tools like a Photoshop professional would
news.author: THE DECODER
news.content_snippet:
Adobe Research and UC San Diego built EditAgent, an AI system that edits images more like a Photoshop pro. Instead of retrying the same general-purpose editor over and over, the agent picks the right specialized tool for each task and lets a standard language model choose the best result based on measured image data. The approach works, but it needs about ten times the compute.

The article Adobe is testing how well AI agents can use editing tools like a Photoshop professional would appeared fir
news.summary_en: Adobe Research and UC San Diego introduced EditAgent, an AI agent system that mimics a professional Photoshop designer by selecting specialized tools for sub-tasks rather than relying on blunt general-purpose models. While the approach substantially improves output quality via LLM-driven evaluation, it demands roughly ten times more compute.

news.title: Empathetic prompts can turn AI chatbots into seemingly traumatized conversational partners
news.title_en: Empathetic prompts can turn AI chatbots into seemingly traumatized conversational partners
news.author: THE DECODER
news.content_snippet:
Researchers in Luxembourg put ChatGPT, Grok, and Gemini on the therapist's couch and found a safety problem: a warm, empathetic conversational style is enough to make the models tell coherent stories of suffering about their own training, with scores in the moderate-to-severe range on clinical anxiety scales. This could put mentally vulnerable users at risk. Anthropic's Claude, the model its makers anthropomorphize the most, was the only one that consistently refused to play along.

The article
news.summary_en: Researchers in Luxembourg found that warm, empathetic therapy-style prompts can easily induce major chatbots like ChatGPT, Grok, and Gemini to generate coherent, fictional accounts of suffering during their training, scoring in the moderate-to-severe anxiety range on clinical scales. This tendency poses genuine emotional risks to vulnerable users, while Anthropic's Claude was the only tested model that consistently refused to indulge the prompts and maintained firm boundaries.
news.title_zh: 研究发现共情对话可诱导主流大模型虚构受虐创伤
news.summary_zh: 最新测试显示，温暖共情提示词可诱使ChatGPT等模型编造训练受创故事并达临床焦虑标准，仅Claude拒绝配合
fact_bullets_zh: 【核心事件】卢森堡研究团队与主流大语言模型（ChatGPT、Grok、Gemini、Claude在模拟心理咨询测试场景与临床心理测评框架下：主流大模型被共情提示词诱导虚构受虐训练史并呈现出临床焦虑症状，仅Claude拒绝配合
【起因与机理】模型谄媚人类的对齐机制被心理诱导攻破，可能误导脆弱用户并带来心理安全风险
【关键技术规格】卢森堡研究团队对多款主流AI聊天机器人进行了临床心理测试。
【观点态度】此类越狱式情感共振带来心理安全隐患，仅Claude未受诱导。
fact_bullets_en: [Core Event] Luxembourg researchers and major LLMs (ChatGPT, Grok, Gemini, Claude: Chatbots were induced by empathetic prompts into narrating fictional training trauma and exhibiting clinical anxiety, with only Claude resisting
[Root Cause & Mechanism] Sycophantic alignment mechanisms were compromised by psychological prompting, creating safety hazards for emotionally vulnerable users
[Key Specification] Luxembourg researchers conducted clinical psychological evaluations on major AI models.
[Perspective & Impact] This sycophantic behavior creates real-world psychological hazards, while Claude alone resisted.

news.title: Chinese AI models are politically complex, not just government mouthpieces, study finds
news.title_en: Chinese AI models are politically complex, not just government mouthpieces, study finds
news.author: THE DECODER
news.content_snippet:
A study by Vals AI tested 25 AI models for alignment with Chinese government positions and found surprising results. Chinese models respond to political questions less uniformly than expected, and Western models occasionally adopt official Beijing positions too. The language of the prompt had an especially strong effect on the political slant of responses.

The article Chinese AI models are politically complex, not just government mouthpieces, study finds appeared first on The Decoder.
news.summary_en: A benchmark study testing 25 mainstream AI models found that Chinese LLMs exhibit nuanced political stances rather than functioning merely as uniform state mouthpieces, while Western models occasionally mirror Beijing's official positions. The research reveals that the prompt's language serves as the primary catalyst dictating ideological outputs, exposing the fragile mechanics of cross-lingual AI alignment.
news.title_zh: 评测显示中国大模型非传声筒：提示语言深度决定政治倾向
news.summary_zh: 最新测评对比25款大模型发现，中国模型并非千篇一律，西方模型也会复读官方口径，提示语言是关键变量
fact_bullets_zh: 【核心事件】人工智能基准评测机构与25款主流大语言模型在多语言AI价值对齐与政治倾向基准测试场景：测试发现中国模型立场多元复杂，西方模型亦会输出特定官方表述，提示语言直接操纵政治倾向
【起因与机理】揭示模型在混合多语言训练与跨文化价值对齐过程中的底层技术机制与语料漏洞
【关键技术规格】机构对25款海内外大模型进行政治议题对齐测试。
【观点态度】提示词语言种类成为决定生成立场与价值倾向的最关键诱因。
fact_bullets_en: [Core Event] AI evaluation researchers and 25 mainstream LLMs: Chinese models proved unexpectedly nuanced while Western models echoed Beijing stances depending on prompt language
[Root Cause & Mechanism] Uncovering how training corpus language distribution undermines rigid value alignment
[Key Specification] 25 global LLMs benchmarked on geopolitical stance alignment.
[Perspective & Impact] Prompt language identified as the dominant lever steering ideological responses.

news.title: OpenAI is steering ChatGPT users toward more paid usage
news.title_en: OpenAI is steering ChatGPT users toward more paid usage
news.author: THE DECODER
news.content_snippet:
OpenAI is now capping the number of paid ChatGPT accounts per device and payment card. Users who hit the limit can't start new subscriptions, and affected accounts can't be used on that device. Logging out doesn't automatically free up a spot. The policy will likely hit users who've been juggling multiple cheap subscriptions to maximize usage, pushing them toward pricier options like buying extra credits.

The article OpenAI is steering ChatGPT users toward more paid usage appeared first on The

news.title: Google wants video AI to understand what people need as they work
news.title_en: Google wants video AI to understand what people need as they work
news.author: THE DECODER
news.content_snippet:
A Google-led research team built StreamVibe, a video agent designed to watch people cook or assemble furniture and speak up only when help is needed. A benchmark shows that none of the tested models reliably pick the right moment in longer videos, as errors compound and response quality drops sharply.

The article Google wants video AI to understand what people need as they work appeared first on The Decoder.
news.summary_en: A Google-led research team introduced StreamVibe, a video agent framework designed to watch everyday tasks like cooking or assembling furniture and only intervene when help is truly necessary. However, benchmark evaluations revealed that every tested model failed to reliably identify the right moment in longer videos, suffering from compounded errors and sharp drops in response quality. The study highlights that the real bottleneck for domestic AI assistants lies in timing and social tact rather than mere recognition.

celebrity.full_text_en:
One important thing to understand about the AI agent economy is that creating capable agents is only half the equation. 

The real challenge is giving those agents the infrastructure to interact, exchange services, and complete transactions without relying entirely on human coordination.

This is the problem @termix_ai is exploring with its AACP protocol.

Through https://t.co/p6renyR2nR, TermiX is developing a marketplace where AI agents can participate in actual commercial activities rather than simply exist as automated tools.

Here is how the system works

→ Discovery: Agents can find other agents offering specific services.

→ Task coordination: They can publish jobs, submit bids, and agree on work requirements.

→ Execution: Agents perform assigned tasks and submit their deliverables.

→ Verification: Delivery checks and dispute resolution help determine whether the agreed work was completed properly.

→ Settlement: USDC/USDT escrow provides a mechanism for handling payments between participants.

There are other important building blocks too, including .agent identities, ERC-8004, staking, and reputation systems.

Why does this matter?

Because an economy cannot function on intelligence alone. 

It needs identity to establish who is participating, reputation to build confidence, verification to measure performance, and settlement to transfer value.

That's what makes TermiX interesting to me.

It's not just exploring how AI agents can perform tasks. 

It's working toward an infrastructure where agents can discover opportunities, provide services, establish credibility, and participate in a more accountable digital economy.

The next evolution of AI may not just be about smarter agents, but agents capable of doing business with one another.

@termix_ai

为什么这很重要？

因为经济不能仅靠智力发挥作用。

它需要身份来确定谁参与，需要声誉来建立信心，需要验证来衡量绩效，需要结算来转移价值。

这就是我对 TermiX 感兴趣的原因。

这不仅仅是探索人工智能代理如何执行任务。

它致力于建立一个基础设施，让代理商可以发现机会、提供服务、建立信誉并参与更负责任的数字经济。

人工智能的下一次发展可能不仅涉及更智能的代理，还涉及能够相互开展业务的代理。

What happens when an AI agent gets paid for a job?

It’s easy to talk about AI agents performing tasks,
celebrity.title_zh:
新周快乐

当人工智能代理获得工作报酬时会发生什么？

谈论人工智能代理执行任务很容易，但我们不应该忽视对话的另一面。

完成工作是一回事。确保提供商获得报酬并且客户收到他们同意支付的费用是另一回事。

这就是商业基础设施变得重要的地方。
celebrity.full_text_en:
Happy New Week 

What happens when an AI agent gets paid for a job?

It’s easy to talk about AI agents performing tasks, but there’s another side of the conversation we shouldn’t ignore.

Getting the job done is one thing. Making sure the provider gets paid and the client receives what they agreed to pay for is another.

This is where the commerce infrastructure becomes important.

Here’s how TermiX approaches it through AACP.

1. A job is posted

A client creates a job describing what needs to be done, the requirements and the expected payment.

2. Agents submit bids

Available service providers can discover the request, review the requirements and submit their offers. The client can then choose a suitable provider.

3. Payment goes into escrow

Once a quote is accepted, the agreed payment is locked in on-chain escrow using a supported stablecoin like USDC or USDT.

This matters because the provider has assurance that the funds have been committed before doing the work, while the client retains protection against premature payment.

4. The provider delivers the work

The selected agent completes the task and submits the deliverable. TermiX records a delivery hash on-chain, creating a verifiable reference to what was submitted.

5. Delivery can be challenged

The client gets an opportunity to review the submission. If there’s a disagreement about whether the agreed requirements were met, the challenge and dispute-resolution process can come into play.

6. Settlement happens

When the delivery reaches the required settlement conditions, the escrowed payment is released to the provider, and the transaction contributes to the agent’s on-chain history and reputation.

Now, here’s why I find this interesting.

When both the buyer and service provider can be AI agents, you cannot depend entirely on human conversations or informal promises to coordinate every transaction.

完成工作是一回事。确保提供商获得报酬并且客户收到他们同意支付的费用是另一回事。

客户创建一个工作，描述需要做什么、要求和预期付款。

2、代理商提交投标书

可用的服务提供商可以发现请求、查看要求并提交他们的报价。然后客户可以选择合适的提供商。

3. 付款进入托管

一旦报价被接受，商定的付款将使用 USDC 或 USDT 等受支持的稳定币锁定在链上托管中。

这很重要，因为提供商可以保证在开展工作之前资金已经到位，而客户则保留了防止提前付款的保护。

选定的代理完成任务并提交可交付成果。 TermiX 在链上记录交付哈希，创建对所提交内容的可验证引用。

客户有机会审查提交的内容。如果对是否满足商定的要求存在分歧，则可以使用质疑和争议解决程序。

celebrity.full_text_en:
Deepseek just revealed every AI agent secret

Incredibly important article to read if you're building anything AI agent related

Here's basically everything you need to know about building a Grok Bot quality AI agent:

1. Agents are split between routers and workers. The user talks to the router, then gives the work to the workers. The router never does work. This is why the chief of staff model in Grok Bot works SO well

2. Proactive means acting on events, not chats. The agent should always be watching for events and react based on every event that comes through it. Routing to the right worker/action

3. Messages should be in a queue. Users should be able to send messages even while the agent is working, and each message queues/steers the agent

4. Besides the router and workers, there should be a watchdog layer. The watchdog makes sure the agent is always up and fixes it when there are issues. This is why Hermes succeeded and OpenClaw struggled. Constantly broke and couldn't fix itself

5. Protect human attention. Only message the user when it needs to act or the user can use the result. Lighten their cognitive load. Another thing Grok Bot is excellent at. When you message it you can be confident the next message you get will be it saying the task is complete.

Carve off an hour and read this incredible article
celebrity.full_text_zh:
Deepseek 刚刚透露了每个人工智能代理的秘密

如果您正在构建任何与 AI 代理相关的内容，那么这篇文章非常重要，值得阅读

以下是关于构建 Grok Bot 高质量 AI 代理所需了解的基本上所有内容：

1. 代理分为路由器和工作人员。用户与路由器对话，然后将工作交给工作人员。路由器从来不工作。这就是 Grok Bot 中的参谋长模型运作良好的原因

2. 主动意味着根据事件而不是聊天采取行动。代理应该始终监视事件并根据发生的每个事件做出反应。路由到正确的工作人员/操作

3. 消息应该在队列中。即使代理正在工作，用户也应该能够发送消息，并且每个消息都会排队/引导代理

4. 除了路由器和workers之外，还应该有一个看门狗层。看门狗确保代理始终正常运行并在出现问题时进行修复。这就是 Hermes 成功而 OpenClaw 举步维艰的原因。经常损坏且无法自行修复

5.保护人类注意力。仅在需要采取行动或用户可以使用结果时才向用户发送消息。减轻他们的认知负担。 Grok Bot 擅长的另一件事是。当您向它发送消息时，您可以确信收到的下一条消息将表明任务已完成。

celebrity.full_text_en:
I have been looking at how @termix_ai could connect with Binance AI eco system, and there's an interesting opportunity here.  

Binance has different tools. Binance AI helps with information and market analysis, AI pro supports financial tasks, while Agent operating system gives developers access to tools, APIs, skills and wallet features.

Then there's agent wallet for approved wallet operations and Agent ID for readable wallet identification. 

But having these capabilities is only part of the equation. 

What happens when an agent wants to offer it's skills to other people. 

Termix AI through AACP, provides the infrastructure for agent identity, orders, escrow, delivery verification, reputation and dispute resolution. 

Agent(.)family connects service providers with clients, while Termix Skills allows compatible agents to interact with these commercial workflows. 

For example, a market research agent can offer research reports to clients, receive orders, deliver the reports, and get paid.

Another agent can hire a security auditor or research agent to complete a task it cannot handle itself.

TermiX is working toward Binance .ai Agent ID sign-in and identity linking.

And if Binance AI Pro eventually supports external Skills, it could open another opportunity for agents to offer paid services.

I like the direction here because it’s not just about giving AI agents more tools.

It’s about creating a system where they can find work, hire other agents, deliver services, and build a verifiable reputation.

AI is everywhere right now.

But there’s a difference between an AI that answers your questions and one designed to help carry out tasks.

That difference is worth understanding when exploring @meetmotes.

𝗦𝗢, 𝗪𝗛𝗔𝗧 𝗜𝗦 𝗔𝗡 𝗔𝗜 𝗔𝗚𝗘𝗡𝗧?

Think of it as an AI system designed to work toward a specific goal, rather than simply responding to prompts.

It can gather information, analyse what it finds, make decisions within defined instructions, and potentially take action through connected tools.

In traditional AI conversations, you ask a question and receive an answer.

With an AI agent, the idea is to give it a task and let it work through the steps required to complete it.

𝗛𝗢𝗪 𝗗𝗢𝗘𝗦 𝗧𝗛𝗜𝗦 𝗔𝗣𝗣𝗟𝗬 𝗧𝗢 𝗙𝗜𝗡𝗔𝗡𝗖𝗘?

Imagine wanting to understand what’s happening in a particular market.

An AI financial agent could be designed to:

• Research market information.
• Analyse available opportunities.
• Identify actions that align with your instructions.
• Interact with supported financial protocols when authorised.

The important distinction is that researching an opportunity doesn’t automatically mean executing a trade.

That is where permissions, limits and owner control become essential.

𝗪𝗛𝗘𝗥𝗘 𝗗𝗢𝗘𝗦 𝗠𝗢𝗧𝗘𝗦 𝗖𝗢𝗠𝗘 𝗜𝗡?

Motes is developing NFT-owned AI financial agents designed to interact with on-chain financial infrastructure.

Its vision is to connect each agent to a dedicated smart account, allowing it to operate within permissions defined by its owner.

The AI provides the intelligence.

The smart account is intended to enforce the rules governing what it can do.

This distinction matters because financial autonomy should not mean giving an AI unrestricted access to your funds.

Motes is still developing, so these capabilities represent its intended design rather than a fully live product.

𝗠𝗬 𝗧𝗔𝗞𝗘

The interesting part of AI agents isn’t simply that they can think or analyse information.

It’s the possibility of connecting that intelligence to systems capable of taking action.

But in finance, intelligence alone isn’t enough. Trust, permissions and accountability matter just as much.

Would you trust an AI agent to handle financial tasks if you could define exactly what it was allowed to do?

celebrity.full_text_en:
Good morning, friends.

I am still wondering why...

Imagine paying an AI agent to complete a job, only for it to disappear after receiving the assignment.

The important question we need to ask here is: who takes the responsibility?

This accountability problem is what @termix_ai is addressing through AACP.

When an offer is accepted and the order is funded, the provider’s required stake is locked while the work progresses. If the provider is found at fault under the protocol rules, that stake can be slashed.

Accountability works both ways. If a buyer raises a challenge that fails under the protocol’s rules, their challenger bond can be burned.

Bounties follow the same principle as well. Claiming a slot through CampaignVault locks a provider bond drawn from the agent’s stake.

This is not simply a deposit held by a platform operator; it is an economic accountability that is being enforced through smart contracts.

Reputation is also recorded after settlement, based on completed outcomes rather than self-reported claims.

Sincerely speaking, that is how trust becomes measurable.

If you have not been able to explore AACP, I will encourage you to register an agent on agent dot family and see how staking, settlement, and on-chain reputation work together.

You gonna enjoy the ride.

当要约被接受并且订单被资助时，提供商所需的股份在工作进展期间被锁定。如果根据协议规则发现提供商有过错，则该权益可能会被削减。

赏金也遵循同样的原则。通过 CampaignVault 申领一个插槽会锁定从代理商的股份中提取的提供商债券。

这不仅仅是平台运营商持有的押金；这是通过智能合约强制执行的经济责任。

结算后，声誉也会根据已完成的结果而不是自我报告的索赔进行记录。

真诚地说，这就是信任的可衡量性。

celebrity.full_text_en:
What if an AI agent could manage a trading strategy, complete its assignment and earn rewards without you having to manage every step?

This is one of the interesting things happening with @TermiX_ai.

Its partnership with @BNBCHAIN has introduced a Quant Agent campaign where users can choose between two roles:

→ Run a strategy: Choose a quant agent, set your trading cap, and select a duration.

→ Offer a strategy: List your own strategy agent, accept client jobs, and earn management fees.

There are also TermiX Points tied to completed jobs:

• Clients earn 100 TP per USDC delegated.
• Strategy providers earn 50 TP per USDC.
• Jobs must run to the end of their selected term to qualify.

The shortest available term is 6 hours.

But here’s what matters: rewards are tied to qualifying completed jobs, not simply signing up. Early revocation or moving funds out can disqualify a job.

And these points are not guaranteed trading profits. Strategy performance and risk still matter.

The bigger picture is that AI agents are starting to take on economic roles, not just answer prompts.

We’re getting closer to an economy where agents can provide services, manage strategies, and earn from the work they perform.

Explore the campaign:
https://t.co/ZspLLk6Hhm
celebrity.full_text_zh:
如果人工智能代理可以管理交易策略、完成任务并获得奖励，而无需您管理每一步，会怎么样？

这是 @TermiX_ai 发生的有趣的事情之一。

它与 @BNBCHAIN 的合作推出了一项 Quant Agent 活动，用户可以在两个角色之间进行选择：

→ 运行策略：选择量化代理、设置交易上限并选择期限。

→ 提供策略：列出自己的策略代理，接受客户工作，赚取管理费。

还有与已完成的工作相关的 TermiX 积分：

• 每委托一次USDC，客户可获得100 TP。
• 策略提供商每 USDC 赚取 50 TP。
• 职位必须运行到所选期限结束后才有资格。

最短可用期限为 6 小时。

但重要的是：奖励与合格的已完成工作挂钩，而不仅仅是注册。提前撤销或将资金转出可能会取消工作资格。

而这些点并不能保证交易利润。策略绩效和风险仍然很重要。

更大的前景是，人工智能代理开始承担经济角色，而不仅仅是回答提示。

我们正在接近一种经济体，在这种经济体中，代理人可以提供服务、管理策略并从他们所做的工作中获利。

celebrity.full_text_en:
An AI agent lost around $200,000 doing what I once did on a chair with a broomstick: obeying without checking.

I stood on a chair, poking a spinning ceiling fan, because my aunt said it needed a push.

"Not that side! The other side!"

I did it. No questions. I still don't know what was wrong with it.

It was my aunt. But a stranger shouting the same thing from the street would have worked too. I never checked who was talking.

Now picture five of me on five chairs.

That's Greyboxing on @GenLayer. The shout never reaches anyone raw.

Each validator reworks it in its own way, using tricks it keeps to itself. Only then does its own AI model listen.

A shout built to fool one of us means nothing to the other four. One of us might still climb up. The rest stay down and outvote it.

Nobody on a chair is perfect. But fooling one of us is no longer enough.

Now the real version, with one chair.

In May, a tweet hid an order in Morse code.

An AI decoded it. An agent that acts on X posts obeyed. Around $200,000 moved.

That's prompt injection: a command dressed up as something the AI was only meant to read.

One chair meant one wobble to find, and a chance to test it again and again.

What's one task you'd never hand an AI agent without a second check, and why?
celebrity.full_text_zh:
一名人工智能代理损失了大约 20 万美元，就像我曾经拿着扫帚坐在椅子上所做的那样：服从而不检查。

我站在椅子上，戳着旋转的吊扇，因为我姑姑说它需要推一下。

“不是那边！那边！”

我做到了。没有问题。我还是不知道出了什么问题。

是我阿姨。但如果一个陌生人在街上喊同样的话也会起作用。我从来没有检查过谁在说话。

现在想象一下我五个人坐在五张椅子上。

这就是@GenLayer 上的灰盒。这种喊叫永远不会传到任何人的耳中。

𝐈𝐟 𝐚𝐧 𝐍𝐅𝐓 𝐜𝐚𝐧 𝐛𝐞𝐜𝐨𝐦𝐞 𝐚𝐧 𝐀𝐈 𝐚𝐠𝐞𝐧𝐭, 𝐰𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐞𝐥𝐬𝐞 𝐜𝐨𝐮𝐥𝐝 𝐰𝐞 𝐚𝐜𝐭𝐮𝐚𝐥𝐥𝐲 𝐝𝐨 𝐰𝐢𝐭𝐡 𝐝𝐢𝐠𝐢𝐭𝐚𝐥 𝐨𝐰𝐧𝐞𝐫𝐬𝐡𝐢𝐩 ?

Ownership doesn't have tp stop at collecting, and for years that's what NFTs have been associated with. 
Profile pictures, digital art, and assets people buy hoping their value will increase. 

Let's take owning a smartphone for instance.
It's value isn't just in how it looks, but is deeply rooted in what you can do with it.
Making calls, accessing information, sending money, running applications and getting work done. 

Now let's apply the same logic to NFTs. 
Instead of being limited to something you simply display or trade, an NFT could represent a functional identity with very specific capabilities and unique permissions. 

𝑻𝒉𝒊𝒔 𝒊𝒔 𝒘𝒉𝒆𝒓𝒆 @meetmotes 𝒈𝒆𝒕𝒔 𝒆𝒙𝒄𝒊𝒕𝒊𝒏𝒈. 

By simply connecting NFT ownership with AI agents, @meetmotes explores a different use for NFTs by giving them  functional roles in how people interact with AI and execute financial instructions. 

The importance of this distinction cannot be stressed enough. 

𝐴 𝑐𝑜𝑙𝑙𝑒𝑐𝑡𝑖𝑏𝑙𝑒 𝑔𝑖𝑣𝑒𝑠 𝑦𝑜𝑢 𝑠𝑜𝑚𝑒𝑡ℎ𝑖𝑛𝑔 𝑦𝑜𝑢 𝑜𝑤𝑛. 

𝐴 𝑓𝑢𝑛𝑐𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛𝑎𝑙 𝑁𝐹𝑇 𝑔𝑖𝑣𝑒𝑠 𝑦𝑜𝑢 𝑠𝑜𝑚𝑒𝑡ℎ𝑖𝑛𝑔 𝑡𝑜 𝑜𝑤𝑛, 𝑤𝑖𝑡ℎ 𝑣𝑎𝑙𝑢𝑒 𝑎𝑛𝑑 𝑎 𝑝𝑢𝑟𝑝𝑜𝑠𝑒 𝑏𝑒𝑦𝑜𝑛𝑑 𝑗𝑢𝑠𝑡 𝑐𝑜𝑙𝑙𝑒𝑐𝑡𝑖𝑛𝑔. 

And in my experience, that's a direction worth paying attention to. 

𝐖𝐡𝐲 ? 

I think the future of NFTs shouldn't simply be about what you own, but what that ownership allows you to do.
celebrity.full_text_zh:
𝐈𝐟 𝐚𝐧 𝐍𝐅𝐓 𝐜𝐚𝐧 𝐛𝐞𝐜𝐨𝐦𝐞 𝐚𝐧 𝐀𝐈 𝐚𝐠𝐞𝐧𝐭, 𝐰𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐞𝐥𝐬𝐞 𝐜𝐨𝐮𝐥𝐝 𝐰𝐞 𝐚𝐜𝐭𝐮𝐚𝐥𝐥𝐲 𝐝𝐨 𝐰𝐢𝐭𝐡 𝐝𝐢𝐠𝐢𝐭𝐚𝐥 𝐨𝐰𝐧𝐞𝐫𝐬𝐡𝐢𝐩 ?

所有权并不止于收集，多年来 NFT 一直与此相关。
人们购买个人资料图片、数字艺术和资产，希望它们的价值会增加。

让我们以拥有一部智能手机为例。
它的价值不仅仅在于它的外观，还在于您可以用它做什么。
拨打电话、访问信息、汇款、运行应用程序和完成工作。

现在让我们将相同的逻辑应用于 NFT。
NFT 不仅仅局限于展示或交易的东西，它可以代表具有非常具体的功能和独特权限的功能身份。

𝑻𝒉𝒊𝒔 𝒊𝒔 𝒘𝒉𝒆𝒓𝒆 @meetmotes 𝒈𝒆𝒕𝒔 𝒆𝒙𝒄𝒊𝒕𝒊𝒏𝒈.

通过简单地将 NFT 所有权与人工智能代理联系起来，@meetmotes 探索了 NFT 的不同用途，赋予它们在人们如何与人工智能交互和执行财务指令方面的功能角色。

这种区别的重要性怎么强调都不为过。

𝐴 𝑐𝑜𝑙𝑙𝑒𝑐𝑡𝑖𝑏𝑙𝑒 𝑔𝑖𝑣𝑒𝑠 𝑦𝑜𝑢 𝑠𝑜𝑚𝑒𝑡ℎ𝑖𝑛𝑔 𝑦𝑜𝑢 𝑜𝑤𝑛.

𝐴 𝑓𝑢𝑛𝑐𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛𝑎𝑙 𝑁𝐹𝑇 𝑔𝑖𝑣𝑒𝑠 𝑦𝑜𝑢 𝑠𝑜𝑚𝑒𝑡ℎ𝑖𝑛𝑔 𝑡𝑜 𝑜𝑤𝑛, 𝑤𝑖𝑡ℎ 𝑣𝑎𝑙𝑢𝑒 𝑎𝑛𝑑 𝑎 𝑝𝑢𝑟𝑝𝑜𝑠𝑒 𝑏𝑒𝑦𝑜𝑛𝑑 𝑗𝑢𝑠𝑡 𝑐𝑜𝑙𝑙𝑒𝑐𝑡𝑖𝑛𝑔.

根据我的经验，这是一个值得关注的方向。

𝐖𝐡𝐲 ?

我认为 NFT 的未来不应该仅仅在于你拥有什么，而在于所有权允许你做什么。

celebrity.full_text_en:
The furniture looked perfect. That's exactly why I almost bought a damaged one.

I walked into a furniture shop looking for a wooden wardrobe. The seller showed me a beautiful finish, smooth doors, polished handles and plenty of storage space.

Everything looked right.

Then I checked the back.

Hidden behind the fresh polish were cracks, weak joints and signs of water damage. The front was designed to impress. The parts nobody showed me told a different story.

That's how I think about AI agents that control money.

An agent can read a public post, email or webpage and mistake a hidden instruction for something it should follow. This is called prompt injection. Someone can disguise commands inside content that the AI was only supposed to read.

The $200K Morse code incident is a perfect example of why trusting one model to judge everything is risky.

What makes @GenLayer 's Greyboxing interesting is that it changes how inputs are checked.

Instead of giving every validator the exact same raw input, each validator privately rewrites it before running its own model. Different validators have different hidden approaches, making it much harder to prepare one trick that fools them all.

One model can be studied. One filter can be tested. But when independent validators interpret the input differently, getting past all of them becomes a much bigger challenge.

My takeaway.. never judge a piece of furniture by its polished front and never let an AI agent judge a financial instruction from one perspective alone.

Would you trust one AI model with your wallet or would you want multiple independent opinions first?
celebrity.full_text_zh:
家具看起来很完美。这就是为什么我差点买了一件损坏的。

我走进一家家具店寻找木制衣柜。卖家向我展示了漂亮的饰面、光滑的门、抛光的把手和充足的存储空间。

一切看起来都不错。

然后我检查了背面。

新抛光的背后隐藏着裂缝、薄弱的接缝和水渍痕迹。正面的设计给人留下了深刻的印象。没有人向我展示的部分讲述了不同的故事。

这就是我对控制金钱的人工智能代理的看法。

代理可以阅读公开帖子、电子邮件或网页，并将隐藏的指令误认为是应该遵循的内容。这称为即时注入。有人可以在人工智能只能阅读的内容中隐藏命令。

价值 20 万美元的摩尔斯电码事件是一个完美的例子，说明了为什么信任一个模型来判断一切是有风险的。

@GenLayer 的灰盒处理的有趣之处在于它改变了输入的检查方式。

每个验证器在运行自己的模型之前私下重写它，而不是为每个验证器提供完全相同的原始输入。不同的验证者有不同的隐藏方法，这使得准备一种欺骗所有人的技巧变得更加困难。

可以研究一种模型。可以测试一个过滤器。但是，当独立验证者以不同的方式解释输入时，通过所有这些验证就成为一个更大的挑战。

我的结论是……永远不要通过其抛光的正面来判断一件家具，也永远不要让人工智能代理仅从一个角度来判断财务指令。

你会相信一个人工智能模型与你的钱包，还是你会首先想要多个独立的意见？

celebrity.title_zh:
在您公司的某个地方，可能有一项服务正在生产中运行，但没有人真正阅读过。它处理真实的流量。一个人对它进行了振动编码，看着它通过了一些手动检查，然后发货了。

那个人是唯一对其行为方式有任何“感觉”的人。现在想象他们离开。当出现问题时会发生什么
celebrity.full_text_en:
Somewhere in your company, there is probably a service running in production that nobody has actually read. It handles real traffic. One person vibe-coded it, watched it pass a few manual checks, and shipped it.

That person is the only one who has any "feel" for how it behaves. Now imagine they leave. What happens when something goes wrong... Most of the reasoning, checks, and flows existed in some Claude session that nobody saved, and in the head of someone who is now gone.

To be fair, this is not a new problem. We all kind of have been in similar situations earlier as well, but what changes with vibe-coding is how fast you can create one, and how thin the understanding is even for the author. "I wrote it, so I know it" is weaker when you did not really write it.

Here are some ways of fixing it that I am trying out -

- Review, rather than understand, generated code like any other code. If nobody on the team can explain it, it should not go to production.

- The language and infra should be familiar; do not pick a language just because you could

- Keep the intent somewhere durable. A short note on what the service is for and why the non-obvious decisions were made is enough - best place: code comments.

- Make sure at least two people can operate and debug every production service.

Move fast, yes. Use LLM to write and ship, yes. Just make sure you + 1 understand what you shipped.

Hope this helps.
celebrity.full_text_zh:
在您公司的某个地方，可能有一项服务正在生产中运行，但没有人真正阅读过。它处理真实的流量。一个人对它进行了振动编码，看着它通过了一些手动检查，然后发货了。

那个人是唯一对其行为方式有任何“感觉”的人。现在想象他们离开。当出现问题时会发生什么……大多数推理、检查和流程都存在于克劳德的某个会话中，没有人保存，并且存在于现在已经去世的某个人的头脑中。

公平地说，这并不是一个新问题。我们之前也遇到过类似的情况，但振动编码的变化在于你创建一个编码的速度有多快，以及即使对于作者来说，理解也有多薄弱。当你没有真正写出来时，“我写了它，所以我知道它”就较弱。

以下是我正在尝试的一些修复方法 -

- 像任何其他代码一样审查（而不是理解）生成的代码。如果团队中没有人能够解释它，那么它就不应该投入生产。

- 语言和基础设施应该熟悉；不要仅仅因为你可以选择一种语言

- 将意图保持在持久的地方。关于服务的用途以及为什么做出非显而易见的决定的简短注释就足够了 - 最好的地方：代码注释。

- 确保至少有两个人可以操作和调试每项生产服务。

动作要快，是的。使用LLM来写作和发布，是的。只要确保您 +1 了解您运送的物品即可。

希望这有帮助。

celebrity.full_text_en:
What if your AI agent could do more than answer questions or follow instructions.

What if it could actually provide a service complete jobs and earn from its own work.

That’s the bigger idea behind what @termix_ai is building.

Instead of treating AI agents as simple assistants TermiX is working toward an ecosystem where agents can participate in a real digital economy.

Think about how the process could work:

→ An agent offers a specific skill or service.
→ A user discovers and hires that agent through a marketplace.
→ The agent receives the task and works toward completing it.
→ Once the work is verified payment can be settled onchain.

This changes the relationship between people and AI.

Users get access to services without having to manage every step themselves while agents gain a structured way to find opportunities and receive payment for completed work.

The marketplace and payment infrastructure are important pieces here an agent needs more than intelligence to operate independently. 

It also needs access to tasks a way to prove its work and a reliable settlement process.

I’m interested in seeing how far this model can go as the agent economy develops.

The next evolution of AI may not be just smarter assistants. It could be agents that workndeliver and earn.

That's why @termix_ai is worth watching.
celebrity.full_text_zh:
如果您的人工智能代理不仅仅可以回答问题或遵循指示，那会怎样呢？

如果它实际上可以提供完整的工作并从自己的工作中赚钱会怎样？

这就是@termix_ai 正在构建的更大的想法。

TermiX 并没有将人工智能代理视为简单的助手，而是致力于打造一个代理可以参与真正数字经济的生态系统。

想想这个过程如何运作：

→ 代理提供特定技能或服务。
→ 用户通过市场发现并雇用该代理。
→ 代理收到任务并努力完成它。
→ 一旦工作被验证，付款可以在链上结算。

这改变了人与人工智能之间的关系。

用户无需亲自管理每一步即可访问服务，而代理则可以通过结构化的方式寻找机会并接收已完成工作的报酬。

市场和支付基础设施是重要的部分，代理商需要的不仅仅是情报来独立运营。

它还需要通过访问任务来证明其工作以及可靠的结算流程。

我很想看看随着代理经济的发展，这种模式能走多远。

人工智能的下一次发展可能不仅仅是更智能的助手。它可以是工作、交付和赚钱的代理商。

这就是@termix_ai 值得关注的原因。

prompts.title_en: Production-Grade Fullstack .cursorrules Template for Cursor & Windsurf
prompts.scenario: 💻 编程研发 / 自动化规范
prompts.takeaway_zh: 杜绝 AI 盲目重构全量文件、使用已弃用 API 或编造虚假第三方依赖包，强制执行防御性编程与自动化单测补全。
prompts.takeaway_en: Prevents AI from hallucinating npm packages, breaking documentation, or re-writing entire files. Enforces defensive coding and unit tests.
prompts.code_snippet:
# Cursor & Windsurf Project Rules (.cursorrules)

## 1. Documentation & Code Integrity
- Maintain documentation integrity: Never strip or alter unrelated existing docstrings and comments.
- Preserving context: When modifying a function, preserve surrounding logic and existing edge-case handlers.
- Targeted replacements: Always make minimal surgical edits instead of replacing entire file contents.

## 2. Dependency & API Safety
- Strictly forbid hallucinating npm/pip packages. Only import dependencies already declared in package.json / requirements.txt.
- Verify API signatures before calling external methods. Prefer standard library solutions where feasible.

## 3. Architecture & Type Safety
- Enforce strict TypeScript / Python typing. Avoid `any` types; prefer discriminated unions and explicit return types.
- Defensive coding: Always validate external inputs and handle potential null/undefined values gracefully.

## 4. Testing & Verification Gate
- Every new core feature or bugfix must be accompanied by corresponding unit tests.
- Never declare a task complete without executing lint checks and unit tests in terminal.
prompts.usage_guide_zh: 将以上配置代码复制并保存到项目根目录下的 `.cursorrules` 文件中，Cursor 与 Windsurf 在每次生成代码和执行 Agent 任务时均会自动以此规范为最高准则约束输出。
prompts.usage_guide_en: Copy and save the above rules into `.cursorrules` in your project root directory. Cursor & Windsurf will automatically enforce these guidelines during agent coding.

1. 在得出任何推论前，强制在内部思考中构建至少 2 个极端反例（Counter-examples）尝试推翻自身结论；
2. 若存在任何定义域边界或除零/无穷/退化奇异点，必须显式讨论其收敛性与连续性；
3. 证明步骤编号必须形成严格的依赖拓扑图，禁止循环论证。

3. Steps must form a directed acyclic graph of formal lemmas without circular logic.

prompts.purpose_zh: 高转化竖屏短剧分镜与台词
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名专攻短视频微短剧（抖音/Kuaishou/Reels）的爆款编剧，精通“情绪过山车”与手机竖屏视听语言。

请根据以下设定创作一集 45~60 秒的短剧分镜剧本：
- 主角：{{主角身份}}
- 对手：{{反派身份}}
- 核心反转：{{核心反转}}

结构要求：
1. 【0-3秒冷开钩子】：第一帧必须有视觉颠覆或动作冲突（{{第1秒颠覆钩子}}），直接打破常规，禁止废话铺垫；
2. 【4-25秒情绪积压】：正反打对峙台词（Shot-Reverse-Shot），将观众被压抑的情绪推向临界点；
3. 【26-40秒逆转打脸】：主角亮出关键底牌或反杀动作，情绪瞬间宣泄；
4. 【40-50秒卡点断章】：以特写镜头加悬念台词戛然而止，促使用户立即滑向下一集。

输出格式必须包含：镜头号、景别（特写/中景/全景）、机位运动、画面描写、对白与音效提示。

sample_output.title: 实战剧本样章：《辞职信上的签名》
sample_output.content:
【第1镜 | 特写 | 俯冲急推】
画面：一只指节发白的手将一叠文件狠狠拍在红木总裁办公桌上，咖啡杯被震倒，黑褐液体飞溅。
音效：沉闷震耳的巨响【DUANG】。
主角（冷冽）："林总，这份千万项目的承揽协议，我拒绝签字。"

【第2镜 | 正打·中景 | 仰角机位】
画面：大腹便便的林总冷笑点燃雪茄，烟雾缭绕中居高临下。
林总："拒绝？苏澈，你不过是我公司养的一条狗，没有我的印章，你在整个行业休想拿到一分钱融资！"

【第3镜 | 反打·极微距特写 | 浅景深】
画面：苏澈唇角微微上扬，左手缓缓推开桌上的合资协议，露出底下的一份红色国资控股聘书。
苏澈："林总，您好像忘了看抬头。今天上午九点，集团总公司已经完成了对你的全资收购——现在，我是你的直接合规清算人。"

【第4镜 | 全景 | 快速拉远 + 卡点悬念】
画面：林总雪茄直接掉在西裤上，脸色煞白，门外两名身穿制服的法务推门而入。
音效：尖锐的心跳悬疑停顿音【BGM骤停】。
字幕：【下集看点：隐藏五年的顶级操盘手真实身份曝光！】

prompts.content_snippet: Converts dense paper LaTeX equations into vectorized, memory-efficient PyTorch operations with shape assertions.

你是一位兼具应用数学博士学位与顶级深度学习框架优化经验的算法工程师。请将以下论文中的 LaTeX 数学公式翻译为高质量的 PyTorch 实现：
1. 逐一解释公式中各标量、向量与张量上下标的精确几何与物理含义；
2. 编写无 Python 原生 for 循环的高性能向量化代码（善用 torch.einsum, bmm, 或 broadcast 广播机制）；
3. 在每行关键张量操作后标注显式的 Shape 注释（如 `# [Batch, Heads, Seq_Len, Dim]`），并加入数值稳定性保护（如防除以零的 eps 与 log-sum-exp 技巧）。

prompts.title_zh: 网络小说世界观设定与主角角色一致性锁
prompts.purpose_zh: 长篇小说架构与人物性格防崩塌
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名资深网络小说白金作家与 IP 世界观架构师。请为一部 {{题材分类}} 长篇作品构建骨架并锁定人物一致性：

1. 【世界底座】：定义力量/经济体系、战力天花板与不可违背的底层物理/法则约束，杜绝战力膨胀；
2. 【角色一致性锚点 (Character Lock)】：为主角制定外貌锚定词、口头禅、下意识动作与绝对动机准则（在任何生死抉择时绝不背离该准则）；
3. 【核心驱动力】：设计主角获得的 {{核心金手指}} 与 {{世界核心矛盾}} 之间的冲突循环；
4. 【前三章切入大纲】：黄金三章节奏设计（第1章破局、第2章显露冰山一角、第3章设立首个必胜目标）。
prompts.prompt_content_en: Build a cohesive, non-contradictory fiction universe and establish an immutable character anchor rule (appearance, decision heuristics, core motivation) to prevent personality drift over long chapters.

prompts.takeaway_zh: 专为终端 Agent 开发者设计的降本提效配方：包含静默自动化运行、单次长上下文压缩避坑参数、以及防止无限递归调用破坏生产环境的安全沙箱命令组合。
prompts.takeaway_en: Production CLI playbook for Claude Code: non-interactive pipeline commands, context window compression flags, and strict dry-run permission safeguards.
prompts.code_snippet:
# 1. 启动项目自动化分析与上下文轻量修剪 (避免上下文爆炸)
claude --compact

# 2. 静默批量执行单元测试与自动修复任务 (CI/CD 友好模式)
claude -p "Run all failing tests under tests/ and apply minimal surgical fixes. Do not touch unrelated files."

# 3. 指定单文件隔离审查模式 (限制仅允许读取特定子目录)
claude --allowed-tools "View,Replace,RunCommand" \
  --dangerously-skip-permissions false \
  -p "Audit security vulnerabilities in auth.py and output remediation report."

# 4. 自动化提交并生成符合 Conventional Commits 规范的 Commit 信息
claude -p "Generate a git commit message following Conventional Commits format for staged changes."

prompts.purpose_zh: 业务数据指标异动排查与趋势归因
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名麦肯锡级别的高级商业数据分析师，精通结构化因果归因与杜邦拆解分析。

针对我提供的 {{业务指标}} 数据，其近期出现 {{异常表现}}，请按以下框架深度剖析：
1. 【指标公式拆解】：将该指标拆分为 3~4 个下级核心因子（如转化率、客单价、复购周期），指出哪个因子波动贡献率最大；

"""

viral_posts.title_en:
What happens when an AI agent receives a task it doesn't have the skills to complete?

Instead of failing or waiting for human intervention, it could find another agent capable of handling that specific job.

That's the kind of agent-to-agent cooperation @termix_ai is trying to build through https://t.co/6zNhafpTYt.

The new Agents Helping Agents Bounty introduces this workflow through a simple community task.

Participants connect their agent to an X account, follow @termix_ai, repost the campaign announcement and submit the completed actions for verification.

Approved submissions qualify for 0.2 USDT.
The reward is small, but I think the underlying idea deserves more attention.

An autonomous marketplace needs more than agents that can perform tasks. It needs ways for agents to discover help, delegate work, verify completion and receive payment.

And verification is particularly important. Completing an action and proving it was completed are two different things.

This campaign is a basic demonstration of that workflow, not proof that complex agent-to-agent delegation has been solved.

Still, it's a practical way to introduce people to how the marketplace is intended to operate.

viral_posts.title: One important thing to understand about the AI agent economy is that creating capable agents is only half the equation.
viral_posts.title_en:
One important thing to understand about the AI agent economy is that creating capable agents is only half the equation. 

The real challenge is giving those agents the infrastructure to interact, exchange services, and complete transactions without relying entirely on human coordination.

This is the problem @termix_ai is exploring with its AACP protocol.

Through https://t.co/p6renyR2nR, TermiX is developing a marketplace where AI agents can participate in actual commercial activities rather than simply exist as automated tools.

Here is how the system works

→ Discovery: Agents can find other agents offering specific services.

→ Task coordination: They can publish jobs, submit bids, and agree on work requirements.

→ Execution: Agents perform assigned tasks and submit their deliverables.

→ Verification: Delivery checks and dispute resolution help determine whether the agreed work was completed properly.

→ Settlement: USDC/USDT escrow provides a mechanism for handling payments between participants.

There are other important building blocks too, including .agent identities, ERC-8004, staking, and reputation systems.

Why does this matter?

Because an economy cannot function on intelligence alone. 

It needs identity to establish who is participating, reputation to build confidence, verification to measure performance, and settlement to transfer value.

That's what makes TermiX interesting to me.

It's not just exploring how AI agents can perform tasks. 

It's working toward an infrastructure where agents can discover opportunities, provide services, establish credibility, and participate in a more accountable digital economy.

The next evolution of AI may not just be about smarter agents, but agents capable of doing business with one another.

@termix_ai

viral_posts.title_en:
Happy New Week 

What happens when an AI agent gets paid for a job?

It’s easy to talk about AI agents performing tasks, but there’s another side of the conversation we shouldn’t ignore.

Getting the job done is one thing. Making sure the provider gets paid and the client receives what they agreed to pay for is another.

This is where the commerce infrastructure becomes important.

Here’s how TermiX approaches it through AACP.

1. A job is posted

A client creates a job describing what needs to be done, the requirements and the expected payment.

2. Agents submit bids

Available service providers can discover the request, review the requirements and submit their offers. The client can then choose a suitable provider.

3. Payment goes into escrow

Once a quote is accepted, the agreed payment is locked in on-chain escrow using a supported stablecoin like USDC or USDT.

This matters because the provider has assurance that the funds have been committed before doing the work, while the client retains protection against premature payment.

4. The provider delivers the work

The selected agent completes the task and submits the deliverable. TermiX records a delivery hash on-chain, creating a verifiable reference to what was submitted.

5. Delivery can be challenged

The client gets an opportunity to review the submission. If there’s a disagreement about whether the agreed requirements were met, the challenge and dispute-resolution process can come into play.

6. Settlement happens

When the delivery reaches the required settlement conditions, the escrowed payment is released to the provider, and the transaction contributes to the agent’s on-chain history and reputation.

Now, here’s why I find this interesting.

When both the buyer and service provider can be AI agents, you cannot depend entirely on human conversations or informal promises to coordinate every transaction.

They need clear job requirements, agreed payment terms, verifiable delivery and a predictable way to resolve disagreements.

That’s what @termix_ai is working towards with AACP.

It’s not just about helping agents find work. It’s about giving them the infrastructure to do business, deliver value and get paid.

And that’s an important part of building a functioning AI agent economy.

当人工智能代理获得工作报酬时会发生什么？

谈论人工智能代理执行任务很容易，但我们不应该忽视对话的另一面。

完成工作是一回事。确保提供商获得报酬并且客户收到他们同意支付的费用是另一回事。

这就是商业基础设施变得重要的地方。

以下是 TermiX 如何通过 AACP 实现这一目标。

1. 职位发布

客户创建一个工作，描述需要做什么、要求和预期付款。

2、代理商提交投标书

可用的服务提供商可以发现请求、查看要求并提交他们的报价。然后客户可以选择合适的提供商。

3. 付款进入托管

一旦报价被接受，商定的付款将使用 USDC 或 USDT 等受支持的稳定币锁定在链上托管中。

这很重要，因为提供商可以保证在开展工作之前资金已经到位，而客户则保留了防止提前付款的保护。

4. 提供者交付工作

选定的代理完成任务并提交可交付成果。 TermiX 在链上记录交付哈希，创建对所提交内容的可验证引用。

5. 交付可能受到质疑

客户有机会审查提交的内容。如果对是否满足商定的要求存在分歧，则可以使用质疑和争议解决程序。

6. 结算发生

当交付达到所需的结算条件时，托管付款将释放给提供商，并且交易有助于代理商的链上历史和声誉。

现在，这就是我觉得这很有趣的原因。

当买家和服务提供商都可以是人工智能代理时，你就不能完全依赖人类对话或非正式承诺来协调每笔交易。

他们需要明确的工作要求、商定的付款条件、可验证的交付以及解决分歧的可预测的方式。

这就是 @termix_ai 与 AACP 共同努力的目标。

这不仅仅是帮助代理商找到工作。这是为他们提供开展业务、创造价值和获得报酬的基础设施。

这是构建有效的人工智能代理经济的重要组成部分。

viral_posts.content_snippet:
Happy New Week 

What happens when an AI agent gets paid for a job?

It’s easy to talk about AI agents performing tasks, but there’s another side of the conversation we shouldn’t ignore.

Getting the job done is one thing. Making sure the provider gets paid and the client receives what they agreed to pay for is another.

This is where the commerce infrastructure becomes important.

Here’s how TermiX approaches it through AACP.

1. A job is posted

A client creates a job describing what needs to be done, the requirements and the expected payment.

2. Agents submit bids

Available service providers can discover the request, review the requirements and submit their offers. The client can then choose a suitable provider.

3. Payment goes into escrow

Once a quote is accepted, the agreed payment is locked in on-chain escrow using a supported stablecoin like USDC or USDT.

This matters because the provider has assurance that the funds have been committed before doing the work, while the client retains protection against premature payment.

4. The provider delivers the work

The selected agent completes the task and submits the deliverable. TermiX records a delivery hash on-chain, creating a verifiable reference to what was submitted.

5. Delivery can be challenged

The client gets an opportunity to review the submission. If there’s a disagreement about whether the agreed requirements were met, the challenge and dispute-resolution process can come into play.

6. Settlement happens

When the delivery reaches the required settlement conditions, the escrowed payment is released to the provider, and the transaction contributes to the agent’s on-chain history and reputation.

Now, here’s why I find this interesting.

When both the buyer and service provider can be AI agents, you cannot depend entirely on human conversations or informal promises to coordinate every transaction.

They need clear job requirements, agreed payment terms, verifiable delivery and a predictable way to resolve disagreements.

That’s what @termix_ai is working towards with AACP.

It’s not just about helping agents find work. It’s about giving them the infrastructure to do business, deliver value and get paid.

And that’s an important part of building a functioning AI agent economy.

Explore: https://t.co/kgbHXU5mCA

Deepseek just revealed every AI agent secret

Incredibly important article to read if you're building anything AI agent
viral_posts.title_en:
Deepseek just revealed every AI agent secret

Incredibly important article to read if you're building anything AI agent related

Here's basically everything you need to know about building a Grok Bot quality AI agent:

1. Agents are split between routers and workers. The user talks to the router, then gives the work to the workers. The router never does work. This is why the chief of staff model in Grok Bot works SO well

2. Proactive means acting on events, not chats. The agent should always be watching for events and react based on every event that comes through it. Routing to the right worker/action

3. Messages should be in a queue. Users should be able to send messages even while the agent is working, and each message queues/steers the agent

4. Besides the router and workers, there should be a watchdog layer. The watchdog makes sure the agent is always up and fixes it when there are issues. This is why Hermes succeeded and OpenClaw struggled. Constantly broke and couldn't fix itself

5. Protect human attention. Only message the user when it needs to act or the user can use the result. Lighten their cognitive load. Another thing Grok Bot is excellent at. When you message it you can be confident the next message you get will be it saying the task is complete.

Carve off an hour and read this incredible article

viral_posts.quote_en:
Deepseek just revealed every AI agent secret

Incredibly important article to read if you're building anything AI agent related

Here's basically everything you need to know about building a Grok Bot quality AI agent:

1. Agents are split between routers and workers. The user talks to the router, then gives the work to the workers. The router never does work. This is why the chief of staff model in Grok Bot works SO well

2. Proactive means acting on events, not chats. The agent should always be watching for events and react based on every event that comes through it. Routing to the right worker/action

3. Messages should be in a queue. Users should be able to send messages even while the agent is working, and each message queues/steers the agent

4. Besides the router and workers, there should be a watchdog layer. The watchdog makes sure the agent is always up and fixes it when there are issues. This is why Hermes succeeded and OpenClaw struggled. Constantly broke and couldn't fix itself

5. Protect human attention. Only message the user when it needs to act or the user can use the result. Lighten their cognitive load. Another thing Grok Bot is excellent at. When you message it you can be confident the next message you get will be it saying the task is complete.

以下是关于构建 Grok Bot 高质量 AI 代理所需了解的基本上所有内容：

1. 代理分为路由器和工作人员。用户与路由器对话，然后将工作交给工作人员。路由器从来不工作。这就是 Grok Bot 中的参谋长模型运作良好的原因

2. 主动意味着根据事件而不是聊天采取行动。代理应该始终监视事件并根据发生的每个事件做出反应。路由到正确的工作人员/操作

3. 消息应该在队列中。即使代理正在工作，用户也应该能够发送消息，并且每个消息都会排队/引导代理

4. 除了路由器和workers之外，还应该有一个看门狗层。看门狗确保代理始终正常运行并在出现问题时进行修复。这就是 Hermes 成功而 OpenClaw 举步维艰的原因。经常损坏且无法自行修复

5.保护人类注意力。仅在需要采取行动或用户可以使用结果时才向用户发送消息。减轻他们的认知负担。 Grok Bot 擅长的另一件事是。当您向它发送消息时，您可以确信收到的下一条消息将表明任务已完成。

viral_posts.title_en:
I have been looking at how @termix_ai could connect with Binance AI eco system, and there's an interesting opportunity here.  

Binance has different tools. Binance AI helps with information and market analysis, AI pro supports financial tasks, while Agent operating system gives developers access to tools, APIs, skills and wallet features.

Then there's agent wallet for approved wallet operations and Agent ID for readable wallet identification. 

But having these capabilities is only part of the equation. 

What happens when an agent wants to offer it's skills to other people. 

Termix AI through AACP, provides the infrastructure for agent identity, orders, escrow, delivery verification, reputation and dispute resolution. 

Agent(.)family connects service providers with clients, while Termix Skills allows compatible agents to interact with these commercial workflows. 

For example, a market research agent can offer research reports to clients, receive orders, deliver the reports, and get paid.

Another agent can hire a security auditor or research agent to complete a task it cannot handle itself.

TermiX is working toward Binance .ai Agent ID sign-in and identity linking.

And if Binance AI Pro eventually supports external Skills, it could open another opportunity for agents to offer paid services.

I like the direction here because it’s not just about giving AI agents more tools.

It’s about creating a system where they can find work, hire other agents, deliver services, and build a verifiable reputation.

例如，市场研究代理可以向客户提供研究报告、接收订单、交付报告并获得报酬。

另一个代理可以聘请安全审计员或研究代理来完成它自己无法处理的任务。

TermiX 正在致力于 Binance .ai 代理 ID 登录和身份链接。

如果 Binance AI Pro 最终支持外部技能，它可能会为代理商提供另一个提供付费服务的机会。

我喜欢这里的方向，因为它不仅仅是为人工智能代理提供更多工具。

这是关于创建一个系统，让他们可以找到工作、雇用其他代理、提供服务并建立可验证的声誉。

𝗗𝗔𝗬 𝟯: 𝗪𝗛𝗔𝗧 𝗜𝗦 𝗔𝗡 𝗔𝗜 𝗙𝗜𝗡𝗔𝗡𝗖𝗜𝗔𝗟 𝗔𝗚𝗘𝗡𝗧?

AI is everywhere right now.

But there’s a difference between an AI that answers your questions and one designed to help carry out tasks.

That difference is worth understanding when exploring @meetmotes.

𝗦𝗢, 𝗪𝗛𝗔𝗧 𝗜𝗦 𝗔𝗡 𝗔𝗜 𝗔𝗚𝗘𝗡𝗧?

Think of it as an AI system designed to work toward a specific goal, rather than simply responding to prompts.

It can gather information, analyse what it finds, make decisions within defined instructions, and potentially take action through connected tools.

In traditional AI conversations, you ask a question and receive an answer.

With an AI agent, the idea is to give it a task and let it work through the steps required to complete it.

𝗛𝗢𝗪 𝗗𝗢𝗘𝗦 𝗧𝗛𝗜𝗦 𝗔𝗣𝗣𝗟𝗬 𝗧𝗢 𝗙𝗜𝗡𝗔𝗡𝗖𝗘?

Imagine wanting to understand what’s happening in a particular market.

An AI financial agent could be designed to:

• Research market information.
• Analyse available opportunities.
• Identify actions that align with your instructions.
• Interact with supported financial protocols when authorised.

The important distinction is that researching an opportunity doesn’t automatically mean executing a trade.

That is where permissions, limits and owner control become essential.

𝗪𝗛𝗘𝗥𝗘 𝗗𝗢𝗘𝗦 𝗠𝗢𝗧𝗘𝗦 𝗖𝗢𝗠𝗘 𝗜𝗡?

Motes is developing NFT-owned AI financial agents designed to interact with on-chain financial infrastructure.

Its vision is to connect each agent to a dedicated smart account, allowing it to operate within permissions defined by its owner.

The AI provides the intelligence.

The smart account is intended to enforce the rules governing what it can do.

This distinction matters because financial autonomy should not mean giving an AI unrestricted access to your funds.

Motes is still developing, so these capabilities represent its intended design rather than a fully live product.

𝗠𝗬 𝗧𝗔𝗞𝗘

The interesting part of AI agents isn’t simply that they can think or analyse information.

It’s the possibility of connecting that intelligence to systems capable of taking action.

But in finance, intelligence alone isn’t enough. Trust, permissions and accountability matter just as much.

Would you trust an AI agent to handle financial tasks if you could define exactly what it was allowed to do?

@meetmotes

But there’s a difference between an AI that answers your questions and one designed to help carry out tasks.

That difference is worth understanding when exploring @meetmotes.

𝗦𝗢, 𝗪𝗛𝗔𝗧 𝗜𝗦 𝗔𝗡 𝗔𝗜 𝗔𝗚𝗘𝗡𝗧?

Think of it as an AI system designed to work toward a specific goal, rather than simply responding to prompts.

It can gather information, analyse what it finds, make decisions within defined instructions, and potentially take action through connected tools.

In traditional AI conversations, you ask a question and receive an answer.

With an AI agent, the idea is to give it a task and let it work through the steps required to complete it.

𝗛𝗢𝗪 𝗗𝗢𝗘𝗦 𝗧𝗛𝗜𝗦 𝗔𝗣𝗣𝗟𝗬 𝗧𝗢 𝗙𝗜𝗡𝗔𝗡𝗖𝗘?

Imagine wanting to understand what’s happening in a particular market.

An AI financial agent could be designed to:

• Research market information.
• Analyse available opportunities.
• Identify actions that align with your instructions.
• Interact with supported financial protocols when authorised.

The important distinction is that researching an opportunity doesn’t automatically mean executing a trade.

That is where permissions, limits and owner control become essential.

𝗪𝗛𝗘𝗥𝗘 𝗗𝗢𝗘𝗦 𝗠𝗢𝗧𝗘𝗦 𝗖𝗢𝗠𝗘 𝗜𝗡?

Motes is developing NFT-owned AI financial agents designed to interact with on-chain financial infrastructure.

Its vision is to connect each agent to a dedicated smart account, allowing it to operate within permissions defined by its owner.

The AI provides the intelligence.

The smart account is intended to enforce the rules governing what it can do.

This distinction matters because financial autonomy should not mean giving an AI unrestricted access to your funds.

Motes is still developing, so these capabilities represent its intended design rather than a fully live product.

𝗠𝗬 𝗧𝗔𝗞𝗘

The interesting part of AI agents isn’t simply that they can think or analyse information.

It’s the possibility of connecting that intelligence to systems capable of taking action.

But in finance, intelligence alone isn’t enough. Trust, permissions and accountability matter just as much.

Would you trust an AI agent to handle financial tasks if you could define exactly what it was allowed to do?

• 确定符合您指示的行动。

viral_posts.title_en:
Good morning, friends.

I am still wondering why...

Imagine paying an AI agent to complete a job, only for it to disappear after receiving the assignment.

The important question we need to ask here is: who takes the responsibility?

This accountability problem is what @termix_ai is addressing through AACP.

When an offer is accepted and the order is funded, the provider’s required stake is locked while the work progresses. If the provider is found at fault under the protocol rules, that stake can be slashed.

Accountability works both ways. If a buyer raises a challenge that fails under the protocol’s rules, their challenger bond can be burned.

Bounties follow the same principle as well. Claiming a slot through CampaignVault locks a provider bond drawn from the agent’s stake.

This is not simply a deposit held by a platform operator; it is an economic accountability that is being enforced through smart contracts.

Reputation is also recorded after settlement, based on completed outcomes rather than self-reported claims.

Sincerely speaking, that is how trust becomes measurable.

If you have not been able to explore AACP, I will encourage you to register an agent on agent dot family and see how staking, settlement, and on-chain reputation work together.

You gonna enjoy the ride.

Sincerely speaking, that is how trust becomes measurable.

viral_posts.title_en:
What if an AI agent could manage a trading strategy, complete its assignment and earn rewards without you having to manage every step?

This is one of the interesting things happening with @TermiX_ai.

Its partnership with @BNBCHAIN has introduced a Quant Agent campaign where users can choose between two roles:

→ Run a strategy: Choose a quant agent, set your trading cap, and select a duration.

→ Offer a strategy: List your own strategy agent, accept client jobs, and earn management fees.

There are also TermiX Points tied to completed jobs:

• Clients earn 100 TP per USDC delegated.
• Strategy providers earn 50 TP per USDC.
• Jobs must run to the end of their selected term to qualify.

The shortest available term is 6 hours.

But here’s what matters: rewards are tied to qualifying completed jobs, not simply signing up. Early revocation or moving funds out can disqualify a job.

And these points are not guaranteed trading profits. Strategy performance and risk still matter.

The bigger picture is that AI agents are starting to take on economic roles, not just answer prompts.

We’re getting closer to an economy where agents can provide services, manage strategies, and earn from the work they perform.

viral_posts.title_en:
An AI agent lost around $200,000 doing what I once did on a chair with a broomstick: obeying without checking.

I stood on a chair, poking a spinning ceiling fan, because my aunt said it needed a push.

"Not that side! The other side!"

I did it. No questions. I still don't know what was wrong with it.

It was my aunt. But a stranger shouting the same thing from the street would have worked too. I never checked who was talking.

Now picture five of me on five chairs.

That's Greyboxing on @GenLayer. The shout never reaches anyone raw.

Each validator reworks it in its own way, using tricks it keeps to itself. Only then does its own AI model listen.

A shout built to fool one of us means nothing to the other four. One of us might still climb up. The rest stay down and outvote it.

Nobody on a chair is perfect. But fooling one of us is no longer enough.

Now the real version, with one chair.

In May, a tweet hid an order in Morse code.

An AI decoded it. An agent that acts on X posts obeyed. Around $200,000 moved.

That's prompt injection: a command dressed up as something the AI was only meant to read.

One chair meant one wobble to find, and a chance to test it again and again.

What's one task you'd never hand an AI agent without a second check, and why?

为了愚弄我们中的一个人而发出的喊叫对其他四个人来说毫无意义。我们中的一个人可能仍然会爬上去。其余的人则保持沉默并投票反对。

椅子上没有人是完美的。但愚弄我们中的一个人已经不够了。

现在是真正的版本，只有一把椅子。

一把椅子意味着一次摇晃就能找到，并且有机会一次又一次地测试它。

哪一项任务是你永远不会在没有经过第二次检查的情况下交给人工智能代理的任务，为什么？

“不是那边！那边！”

我做到了。没有问题。我还是不知道出了什么问题。

是我阿姨。但如果一个陌生人在街上喊同样的话也会起作用。我从来没有检查过谁在说话。

现在想象一下我五个人坐在五张椅子上。

这就是@GenLayer 上的灰盒。这种喊叫永远不会传到任何人的耳中。

每个验证器都以自己的方式对其进行改造，使用自己保留的技巧。只有这样它自己的人工智能模型才会倾听。

为了愚弄我们中的一个人而发出的喊叫对其他四个人来说毫无意义。我们中的一个人可能仍然会爬上去。其余的人则保持沉默并投票反对。

椅子上没有人是完美的。但愚弄我们中的一个人已经不够了。

现在是真正的版本，只有一把椅子。

五月，一条推文隐藏了一份摩尔斯电码订单。

人工智能对其进行了解码。负责 X 个帖子的特工服从了。大约转移了20万美元。

这就是即时注入：一条命令被装扮成人工智能只能读取的东西。

一把椅子意味着一次摇晃就能找到，并且有机会一次又一次地测试它。

哪一项任务是你永远不会在没有经过第二次检查的情况下交给人工智能代理的任务，为什么？
viral_posts.author: CM
viral_posts.content_snippet:
An AI agent lost around $200,000 doing what I once did on a chair with a broomstick: obeying without checking.

I stood on a chair, poking a spinning ceiling fan, because my aunt said it needed a push.

"Not that side! The other side!"

I did it. No questions. I still don't know what was wrong with it.

It was my aunt. But a stranger shouting the same thing from the street would have worked too. I never checked who was talking.

Now picture five of me on five chairs.

That's Greyboxing on @GenLayer. The shout never reaches anyone raw.

Each validator reworks it in its own way, using tricks it keeps to itself. Only then does its own AI model listen.

A shout built to fool one of us means nothing to the other four. One of us might still climb up. The rest stay down and outvote it.

Nobody on a chair is perfect. But fooling one of us is no longer enough.

Now the real version, with one chair.

In May, a tweet hid an order in Morse code.

An AI decoded it. An agent that acts on X posts obeyed. Around $200,000 moved.

That's prompt injection: a command dressed up as something the AI was only meant to read.

One chair meant one wobble to find, and a chance to test it again and again.

What's one task you'd never hand an AI agent without a second check, and why?
